Write tables to a styled Excel workbook

Source: R/office.R
phw_write_xlsx.Rd

Writes one or more data frames to an .xlsx file in the PHW style, one sheet each: a title row, a navy header, thousands separators, sensible column widths, frozen header row and a source note under the table. Summary tables from phw_summary_table(), phw_group_table() and friends keep their bold group rows and indented levels.

Usage

phw_write_xlsx(
  x,
  file,
  title = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  caption_args = list(),
  digits = 1,
  header_fill = phw_colours[["navy"]],
  font = "Arial",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A data frame, or a named list of data frames (one sheet each; the names become the sheet names).

file

Path of the .xlsx file.

title

Title for the first row of each sheet: one string, or one per sheet. NULL for none.

source, date

Passed to phw_caption() and written under each table.

caption_args

List of other phw_caption() arguments.

digits

Decimal places for non-integer numbers.

header_fill

Header fill colour.

font

Font name. Excel uses it if it is installed on the reader's computer, so Arial is the safe default.

overwrite

Replace file if it exists?

Value

The path to the file, invisibly.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("openxlsx2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
  phw_write_xlsx(list(Cars = head(mtcars), Iris = head(iris)), f,
                 title = "Example tables", source = "Example data")
}
